title: Net expected value now shows minus the whole pursuit cost on resolved and closed cases
failure: A case at resolved or closed_written_off, with a pursuit estimate of $45.00 and every line moved on to payer approved or recovered, has actionableNowCents 0. The case page (cases/[caseId]/page.tsx:115) then shows 'Net expected value -$45.00 (actionable less the pursuit cost)'. The same happens on a partially resolved case whose figure dropped below the whole case's estimate, because the estimate was made for every line. The arithmetic is right; the figure misleads on a case nobody is still pursuing.
fix: In caseSummary, set netExpectedCents to null when row.state is 'resolved' or 'closed_written_off', so the page shows '—'. Keep netExpectedValue(actionable_now_cents, pursuit) for the cases still being worked, as ADR 0082 Decision 5 says. Add that one sentence to Decision 5.
rule: CLAUDE.md four rules (code computes every number, shown with its meaning); ADR 0082 Decision 5

verdict.reasoning:
The finding holds for resolved and closed cases. It does not hold for partially resolved cases.

What happens on a resolved or closed case:
- apps/web/src/lib/triage/queries.ts:377 now computes `netExpectedValue(parseCents(row.actionable_now_cents), pursuit)`. At base 43565235 it used `row.actionable_cents`, the stored total for the whole case. So this PR introduces the change.
- `ACTIONABLE_NOW_OF` (apps/worker/src/triage/actionable-now.ts:69-80) sums only lines that are still at stage actionable with current pricing. On a case at resolved or closed_written_off, every line has moved on or been written off, so the sum is 0.
- `pursuit_cost_cents` is written when the case is inserted (apps/worker/src/triage/execute.ts:449) and is never cleared.
- `netExpectedValue` (packages/triage/src/cases.ts:88) returns actionable minus pursuit. The result is -pursuit.
- The case page at apps/web/src/app/p/[practiceId]/cases/[caseId]/page.tsx:115-125 shows that figure as "Net expected value -$45.00 (actionable less the pursuit cost)". It shows '—' only when the value is null.

A case that recovered money therefore reads as a $45 expected loss. Before this PR the same row showed a positive figure. ADR 0082 Decision 5 (line 85) and its Consequences (line 147) accept a negative figure "when nothing is left to pursue". That makes sense for a case someone is still working: it tells them not to pursue it. The ADR says nothing about resolved or closed cases, where nobody is pursuing anything.

Why the partially resolved part fails: the finding says the estimate "was made for every line". It was not. `pursuitCost()` (cases.ts:77-85) is a fixed estimate per case: the staff rate times (minutesPerPacket + minutesPerFollowUp). A partially resolved case is still being worked and still costs that follow-up. A low or negative net figure there is the intended signal.

Severity: nit is right. The arithmetic and its label are correct, and no stored figure, ledger figure or recovered amount is wrong. Only the text on the page misleads.

Checked and sound:
- The live figure is right for cases still being worked.
- '—' when no estimate exists works, and the Pursuit cost row above it explains why.
- The audit report's per-case "Net expected" column (apps/worker/src/report/content.ts:906) behaves the same way. That code predates this PR, so it is out of scope here.

Better fix: the proposed fix nulls the figure, but the page then shows a bare '—'. That '—' already means "not estimated", so a reader cannot tell the two cases apart. Each '—' should say why.
verdict.fix:
1. apps/web/src/lib/triage/queries.ts:377: compute the figure only for cases still being worked:
`const closed = row.state === 'resolved' || row.state === 'closed_written_off';`
`const net = closed ? null : netExpectedValue(...as now...);`

2. Add `netExpectedState: 'closed' | 'unestimated' | 'live'` to CaseSummary.

3. apps/web/src/app/p/[practiceId]/cases/[caseId]/page.tsx:116: render the '—' with its reason:
- closed: "— (the case is resolved or closed; nothing is left to pursue)"
- unestimated: "— (not estimated)"
- live: keep the current Money figure and label.

4. Add a sentence to ADR 0082 Decision 5 and to the Consequences line 147: "On a resolved or closed case it is not shown: nothing is being pursued."

5. Add a test case to `home-figures.db.test.ts` or the case-page e2e: a resolved case with a pursuit estimate has netExpectedCents null and shows the closed text.

6. Leave partially_resolved cases on the live rule.

7. Optionally, in a separate PR, apply the same rule to the per-case net column of the audit report (report/content.ts:906).

title: The Recovered tile's since-date can come from a deposit or posting that was later reversed, or from the reversal itself, so it can be months earlier than any recovery still standing
failure: The practice proves at deposited. On 2026-01-10 a deposit of $50.00 is matched to the wrong line by hand, and reverseMatch reverses it on 2026-01-11. The first real deposit, $12.00, is dated 2026-08-01. ledgerTotals' entryIds.recovered includes the reversed deposit 'w' and its reversal 'u', because countedStage gives a reversal its target's stage. firstOn takes the earliest effectiveOn over that set, so it returns 2026-01-10. verdict.reasoning:
I tried to refute this and could not. I confirmed it by reading the code at 87691be4 in my own clone (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-PhysicalTherapy/e9e32b44-ea9a-56f5-83b4-9164e617462b/scratchpad/vR1). I did not run a new probe because each step below is a direct reading.

So both a reversed deposit and its reversal are in toDate.entryIds.recovered.

2. **firstOn takes the earliest of them.** apps/worker/src/reconcile/statements.ts:69-71 sets firstOn to the minimum effectiveOn over that whole set, with no check for whether the entry still stands.

3. **The home shows that date.** apps/web/src/lib/dashboard/queries.ts:164 passes it on as recoveredSince, and apps/web/src/components/dashboard/headline.tsx:46-47 renders "to date, since <date>".

4. **The input is realistic.** reverseMatch (apps/worker/src/reconcile/manual.ts:177) is the documented way to undo a wrong manual match. It inserts offsetting 'reversed' entries and leaves the original entry with its early effectiveOn. A deposit matched by hand in January and reversed the next day, followed by the first real deposit in August, gives "since <January date>" next to a total that only counts August cash. That misstates the period the tile names, which is the purpose of UX-003 and HOM-02 ("since its first counted entry").

5. **The fully reversed case is pinned by a test.** recovered-periods.test.ts:95-102 expects recovered '0' with firstOn '2026-09-30'. The tile then reads "$0.00, to date, since 2026-09-30" when nothing stands, where it should read "nothing posted yet".

6. **The property test cannot catch it.** Its oracle, firstRecovered (recovered-periods.test.ts:64-68), uses the same countedStage rule, so it agrees with the bug.

**Checked and sound:** all the dollar figures. toDate and period recovered, and payer approved, match practiceLedgerTotals' composition.

**Severity:** should-fix is right. No amount is wrong. The date is misleading, but it is a secondary label and needs a reversal that comes before the first standing entry.

**Fix:** the proposed fix is sound and is the best option. It uses the same reversedIds idiom that manual.ts:203 already uses. It needs no change to packages/ledger, and adjustments are excluded safely because they always come after their target. One possible improvement is not worth it: also excluding an entry that adjustments have reduced to zero. That is rare, and the database keeps every entry between zero and its evidence.

In recoveredPeriods (apps/worker/src/reconcile/statements.ts:69-71), take firstOn only from counted original entries that still stand:

```ts
const standing = (e: LedgerEntry) => counted.has(e.id) && e.stage !== 'reversed' && e.stage !== 'adjusted' && !reversedIds.has(e.id);
const firstOn = all.filter(standing).reduce<string | null>((first, e) => (first === null || e.effectiveOn < first ? e.effectiveOn : first), null);
```

- Make the oracle firstRecovered in recovered-periods.test.ts:64-68 use the same standing rule.
- At :89, replace the null-iff-empty assertion with "firstOn is null iff no standing counted entry exists".
- Change the expectation at :101 to firstOn null.

- Fix the RecoveredPeriods.firstOn doc comment at :56.
